questions.prompt: Drew Brees spent the first five seasons of his NFL career with a franchise from this city after being drafted in 2001

questions.prompt: This city's team sold Babe Ruth to the Yankees in 1920 to help finance a Broadway play

answer.story: Red Sox owner Harry Frazee sold Ruth to the Yankees on December 26, 1919 partly to fund his Broadway theater investments. Boston had won 5 World Series before the sale and didn't win another until 2004, ending an 86-year drought known as the Curse of the Bambino.

questions.prompt: Connor McDavid recorded 285 points in just 166 OHL games while playing junior hockey in this city

answer.name: Erie, PA
answer.story: Erie selected McDavid #1 in the 2012 OHL Priority Selection after he received Exceptional Player status at age 15. Over 3 seasons he scored 97 goals and 188 assists, winning back-to-back OHL Player of the Year awards before going #1 to the Edmonton Oilers in the 2015 NHL Draft.

questions.prompt: Rory McIlroy's father worked nights behind a bar to help fund his son's golf career in this small town

Rory turned pro at 18 and won 5 major championships including the 2025 Masters to complete the career grand slam.

questions.prompt: Pascal Siakam trained for the Catholic priesthood for 7 years before discovering basketball in this city

answer.name: Douala, Cameroon
answer.story: Siakam's father enrolled him at St. Andrew's Catholic Seminary in Bafia at age 11. His older brothers played NCAA basketball in the US and introduced Pascal to the sport. questions.prompt: 4-tme Pro Bowler and Cowboys QB Dak Prescott grew up in this quiet rural town

answer.story: Dak was born in Sulphur, LA but raised in Haughton. His mom Peggy worked as a truck stop manager. Dak and his siblings lost her to colon cancer in 2013 during his college career.

questions.prompt: Scottie Pippen was a 6'1 backup PG in High School who grew 7 inches at this college

answer.name: Central Arkansas (Conway, AR)
answer.story: Pippen arrived at UCA as a 6'1 walk-on team manager. He grew 7 inches during college and became a 6'8 star. He won 6 NBA titles with MJ and became a HoFer in 2010.

questions.prompt: Alex Honnald free solo climbed El Capitan which sits in the north side of this valley

answer.name: Yosemite Valley, CA
answer.story: Honnold free soloed El Capitan's Freerider route on June 3, 2017 — climbing 3,000 ft of vertical granite with no ropes in 3:56. The film 'Free Solo' won the 2019 Oscar for best documentary.

questions.prompt: USMNT striker Folarin Balogun was this European club's top scorer in 2025-26

answer.name: Monte Carlo, Monaco
answer.story: Balogun scored 19 goals in all comps for Monaco in 2025-26. He was voted club MVP. He was born in NYC, but raised in London. He joined Monaco in '23 for €30M.

questions.prompt: Before he became the NHL's all-time leading goal scorer, Alex Ovechkin was born and raised here

answer.name: Moscow, Russia
answer.story: Ovechkin broke Gretzky's 894 NHL goals record on April 6, 2025. Born in Moscow Sept 17, 1985, he's the son of an Olympic basketball gold medalist mom.

questions.prompt: 5x All-Star, Reggie Miller, spent all 18 NBA seasons playing for this city's team

answer.name: Indianapolis, IN
answer.story: Reggie scored the most in Pacers history. His '8 points in 8.9 seconds' at MSG ('95 Game 1 vs Knicks) is one of the most iconic playoff moments ever.

questions.prompt: After struggling in 2020, the Cubs non-tendered Kyle Schwarber. He signed a one-year contract here

answer.name: Nationals Park (Washington, DC)
answer.story: Schwarber signed a 1 year $10M deal wth the Nats. He hit .253 with 25 HRs in 72 games before being traded to Boston at the July deadline.

questions.prompt: Tim Tebow, the first ever sophomore Heisman winner, won the '06 & '08 national titles for this university

answer.name: Florida (Gainesville, FL)
answer.story: Tebow won the '07 Heisman as a sophomore and led Florida to the '08 BCS title. The Promise speech after a '09 loss inspired a 22-game win streak. Denver drafted him 25th overall in 2010.

questions.prompt: Carlos Alcaraz became tennis's youngest world #1 ever at 19. He grew up in this vibrant town

answer.name: Murcia, Spain
answer.story: Alcaraz won the '22 US Open and hit #1 in the same week. He's trained with Juan Carlos Ferrero (former world #1) since age 15.

questions.prompt: The '98 Winter Olympics was the first to include NHL pros. It was hosted in this Asian city

answer.name: Nagano, Japan
answer.story: Czech Republic upset Russia for hockey gold, with Dominik Hašek as the hero. The Nagano Games introduced curling + snowboarding to the Olympic program.

questions.prompt: Kevin Durant won NBA Rookie of the Year with a franchise from this city after being drafted 2nd overall in 2007

answer.name: Seattle, WA
answer.story: Durant was drafted by the Seattle SuperSonics in June 2007 and averaged 20.3 PPG as a rookie. The franchise relocated to Oklahoma City in summer 2008, becoming the Thunder. Seattle has been without an NBA team ever since.

questions.prompt: Since 2017, college football fans in this city have waved to children watching from a hospital overlooking the stadium

answer.name: Iowa City, IA
answer.story: The Hawkeye Wave began at Kinnick Stadium after a fan suggested the idea on Facebook. At the end of every first quarter, 70,000 fans, players, and coaches turn to the 12th floor of the Stead Family Children's Hospital to wave at pediatric patients gathered at the windows.

questions.prompt: In 1905, Honus Wagner became the first baseball player to sign a bat endorsement deal with a company from this city

answer.name: Louisville, KY
answer.story: On September 1, 1905, Wagner signed with J.F. Hillerich & Son (later Hillerich & Bradsby) to put his autograph on Louisville Slugger bats. It was the first endorsement deal between any athlete and a sporting goods company. The Pirates shortstop had used Hillerich bats since his Louisville Colonels days.

questions.prompt: Before being stripped of all his titles, Lance Armstrong won cycling's biggest race 7 times, all finishing in this city

answer.name: Paris, France
answer.story: The Tour de France has finished on the Champs-Élysées every year since 1975. Armstrong crossed the line first from 1999 to 2005 but was stripped of all seven titles by the UCI in October 2012 after a DA investigation. The record books show seven blank years.

questions.prompt: Muhammad Ali's famous "Rumble in the Jungle" victory over George Foreman took place in this African capital

answer.name: Kinshasa, DR Congo
answer.story: The fight took place on October 30, 1974, at the 20th of May Stadium (now Stade Tata Raphaël) at 4am local time to hit US prime time. Ali used his 'rope-a-dope' tactic to tire Foreman before knocking him out in the 8th round. Promoter Don King secured $5m purses for both fighters from Zaire's President Mobutu.

questions.prompt: Michael Redd, the 2nd round pick who became an All-Star and '08 Olympic champ, grew up & played college here

answer.name: Columbus, OH
answer.story: Redd starred at Ohio State in his hometown, then waited behind Ray Allen before erupting in Milwaukee. He once hit 8 threes in a single quarter and dropped 57 points in 2006, then a Bucks record.

questions.prompt: The Pro Football Hall of Fame has enshrined the NFL's all-time greats here since opening in 1963

answer.name: Canton, OH
answer.story: Canton was chosen because the NFL was founded here in 1920, inside a Hupmobile car dealership. The first class of 1963 included Jim Thorpe, Red Grange, and Sammy Baugh.

questions.prompt: John Stockton, the NBA's all-time leader in both assists and steals, grew up and played college ball in this city

answer.name: Spokane, WA
answer.story: Stockton spent all 19 NBA seasons with the Jazz and owns the career records for assists (15,806) and steals (3,265). He starred at hometown Gonzaga before Utah drafted him in 1984.

questions.prompt: Bobby Orr revolutionized hockey & won 8 straight Norris Trophies as a D-man. He's from this small town

answer.name: Parry Sound, ON
answer.story: Orr won 2 Stanley Cups + 3 Hart Trophies w/ Boston. His 1970 flying Cup-winning OT goal photo is one of sports' most iconic. Knees forced him to retire at 30. HoFer in '79.

questions.prompt: Diego Maradona, scorer of the 'Hand of God' and 'Goal of the Century' in 1986, grew up near this capital

answer.name: Buenos Aires, Argentina

questions.prompt: Before he reinvented the pass rush, Lawrence Taylor was an All-American at this university

questions.prompt: Dr. J spent his first 5 pro seasons in the ABA. He started his career at this port city

answer.name: Norfolk, VA

questions.prompt: Before winning 4 championships, Shaquille O'Neal was born in this city before moving away as a boy

answer.name: Newark, NJ

questions.prompt: Every Olympic torch relay begins each Games at the original ancient stadium in this European city

answer.name: Olympia, Greece
answer.story: Olympia hosted the original Greek Olympics from 776 BC to 393 AD. The modern torch ceremony has started here since 1936. The Hera Temple lights the flame using a parabolic mirror + the sun.

questions.prompt: 8-time Ballon d'Or winner, Lionel Messi, moved from Argentina at 13 to join an academy in this city

answer.name: Barcelona, Spain
answer.story: Barcelona agreed to fund Messi's growth-hormone treatment, so at 13 he left Rosario for its La Masia academy. He became the club's record scorer with 672 goals and won 4 Champions Leagues there.

questions.prompt: After just 1 season, the team that played here traded Brett Favre to the Packers

answer.name: Atlanta, GA

questions.prompt: Before winning 3 majors, Jordan Spieth led this university to the 2012 National Title

answer.name: University of Texas (Austin, TX)

questions.prompt: Nomar Garciaparra was traded to this city just months before the Red Sox won their first World Series in 86 years

questions.prompt: 5x NBA All-Star, Al Horford, was born in this city known for its cruise destination status

questions.prompt: In the 2010 Olympics, Lindsey Vonn became the first American woman to win downhill gold, racing at this resort

questions.prompt: Giannis Antetokounmpo made his pro debut at 16 years old for this club

questions.prompt: The Sharks have played at this arena nicknamed the 'Shark Tank' since 1991

questions.prompt: The largest stadium in the United States, The Big House, packs over 107,000 into this college town

questions.prompt: The Mets won the World Series in '69 and '86 while playing at Shea Stadium which sits here

questions.prompt: Before relocating to become the Hurricanes in 1997, the NHL's Whalers spent 18 seasons here

questions.prompt: A kickoff-return lateral, dubbed the 'Music City Miracle', stunned the Bills in the 2000 playoffs in this city

questions.prompt: Before reaching the NBA, Duncan Robinson starred for a tiny D III school in this New England town

questions.prompt: Every September, Arthur Ashe Stadium hosts the US Open Tennis final in this borough

questions.prompt: In 2024, the NFL played its first South American game at the home of soccer giant Corinthians, in this city

questions.prompt: Hobbled Kirk Gibson hit a pinch-hit walk-off homer in the 1988 World Series opener in this city

questions.prompt: The last major league park to install lights, in 1988, hosted only day games for decades in this city

questions.prompt: Ten Cent Beer Night in 1974 turned into a drunken riot and a forfeit for the MLB team who plays here

questions.prompt: The '94 Winter Olympics was the first to be held separately from the Summer Games. They were in this town

questions.prompt: Cuban flamethrower Aroldis Chapman, owner of the fastest pitch in MLB history, hails from this city

questions.prompt: The Twins and Vikings shared a stadium that was demolished and replaced by the Mall of America in this city

questions.prompt: Barry Bonds was drafted by the Giants in 1982 but didn't sign, heading to college on this campus instead

questions.prompt: Fans wave foam tomahawks and perform a chopping arm motion set to a chant at home games for the baseball team here

questions.prompt: Losing on purpose to stockpile draft picks spawned the rallying cry 'Trust the Process' for the NBA team here

questions.prompt: Premier League Golden Boot winner, Son Heung-min, was born in 1992 in this lakeside city

questions.prompt: An NBA team launched here in 1995 with a Jurassic Park inspired logo

questions.prompt: A blue and gold pro basketball team rooted in the ABA, with a panther mascot named Boomer, plays home games here

questions.prompt: The famous 'Pine Tar Game' ejection over an illegal bat sparked an on-field protest for the MLB team from this city

questions.prompt: The NHL team who plays in this city adopted a leaping orca killer-whale logo in 1997

questions.prompt: Maria Sharapova, a 5-time Grand Slam champion who won Wimbledon at 17 was born in this Siberian city

questions.prompt: One of the 2 schools who remained in the shrunken Pac-12 last year wears crimson and gray and calls this town home

questions.prompt: The NHL franchise that abandoned Quebec City in 1995 is now based in this American city

answer.name: Denver, CO

questions.prompt: The 2026 Tour de France opened not in France, but with a team time trial in this Mediterranean city

questions.prompt: Ryan Fox just won the 2026 Open Championship at Royal Birkdale, a links course on the coast near this town

questions.prompt: Long before Spain's 2026 World Cup victory, the first ever World Cup was staged here in 1930

questions.prompt: A pipe-smoking leprechaun and a parquet floor beneath a rafter full of banners define the team who plays here

questions.prompt: A full-size locomotive chugs on a track above left field, tooting after home runs, at this big league ballpark

questions.prompt: This NHL team plays here, in what's known as 'The State of Hockey'

questions.prompt: The NFL played its first regular-season game in this city in September 2025 at a stadium best known for the Gaelic-games

answer.name: Dublin, Ireland

questions.prompt: The 2023 NBA MVP, a dominant 7-foot center, was born in 1994 in the hilly capital city of this African nation

questions.prompt: Today's Milwaukee Brewers began in 1969. They went by the 'Pilots' and lasted just 1 season in this city

questions.prompt: A gold rally cloth called the 'Terrible Towel,' twirls above crowd at pro football games in this city

questions.prompt: The NBA has staged annual regular-season games at Arena CDMX since 2017 in this sprawling Latin American capital

answer.story: Johnny Manziel's Texas A&M stunned No. 1 Alabama 29-24 in Tuscaloosa in 2012. The redshirt freshman, nicknamed Johnny Football, became the first freshman to win the Heisman Trophy.

questions.prompt: Owner Bill Foley vowed this city's NHL expansion team would win the Stanley Cup in six seasons, then delivered in 2023

answer.name: Las Vegas, NV
answer.story: Bill Foley promised the Vegas Golden Knights would win a Stanley Cup within six seasons of their 2017 debut. The Las Vegas team delivered in 2023, beating Florida in the Final.

questions.prompt: This city's pyramid-shaped NBA arena became a giant Bass Pro Shops store with an indoor swamp and live alligators

answer.name: Memphis, TN
answer.story: The Grizzlies played in Memphis's steel-clad Pyramid from 2001 to 2004. In 2015, the former arena reopened as a Bass Pro Shops megastore with an indoor cypress swamp and live alligators.

questions.prompt: Fidel Castro watched the Orioles play in this capital in 1999, marking MLB's first game in the country in 40 years

answer.name: Havana, Cuba
answer.story: In March 1999, the Baltimore Orioles played Cuba's national team in Havana as Fidel Castro looked on. It was MLB's first game in Cuba in 40 years, part of a brief sports thaw between the nations.

questions.prompt: Nikola Jokić returned from a carriage ride to find his coaches celebrating his 2022 MVP award in this city where he grew up

answer.name: Sombor, Serbia
answer.story: In Sombor, Nuggets coaches and executives surprised Nikola Jokić after a carriage ride to celebrate his second straight MVP. They brought a special commemorative trophy marking the award.

questions.prompt: Brian Windhorst earned the nickname 'LeBron Whisperer' after covering his rise to the nation's #1 prospect at this school

answer.name: St. Vincent-St. Mary High School (Akron, OH)
answer.story: Reporter Brian Windhorst covered teenage LeBron James at St. Vincent-St. Mary High in Akron, Ohio, as he became the nation's top prospect. The deep access earned him the 'LeBron Whisperer' tag.

questions.prompt: Gerald Ford won 2 national titles at this university before turning down multiple NFL teams and attending law school

answer.name: University of Michigan (Ann Arbor, MI)
answer.story: Ford played on the University of Michigan's 1932 and 1933 national champions in Ann Arbor. He declined offers from the Lions and Packers, coached at Yale, and entered Yale Law School in 1938.

questions.prompt: 22 years after stunning the Soviets, the 'Miracle on Ice' team reunited to light the 2002 Olympic cauldron in this city

answer.name: Salt Lake City, UT
answer.story: In 2002, members of the 1980 Miracle on Ice hockey team jointly lit the Olympic cauldron at the Salt Lake City Winter Games, 22 years after their shock win over the Soviet Union.

questions.prompt: On a 1990 NFL preseason trip, a Rams player took home pieces of this city's famous wall, which had fallen months earlier

answer.name: Berlin, Germany
answer.story: The Rams played the Chiefs in Berlin in August 1990, nine months after the Wall opened. Rams lineman Irv Pankey brought home pieces of the Wall and a hat traded with a Soviet soldier.

questions.prompt: Roger Federer and Rafael Nadal launched the 2011 tennis season by rallying on a floating court in this capital's bay

answer.name: Doha, Qatar
answer.story: To open the 2011 season, Roger Federer and Rafael Nadal rallied on a floating pontoon court in the bay of Doha, Qatar, before the Qatar Open. The stunt drew striking photos on the Gulf waters.

questions.prompt: The Vikings' first loss on Sunday ensured that this city's NFL team will remain alone in the 'perfect season' club

answer.name: Miami, FL
answer.story: Every year, the last undefeated NFL team's first loss gives members of the 1972 Dolphins a reason to celebrate: Their perfect season remains unmatched.

questions.prompt: This city is home to AP Top 5 teams in men's and women's basketball, a feat only UConn can match as play gets underway

answer.name: Durham, NC
answer.story: Duke is No. 2 in the men's AP Poll and No. 4 in the women's. UConn has the reverse: No. 4 men, No. 2 women.

questions.prompt: 30 years ago today, Kobe Bryant made his NBA debut just months after graduating high school in this Main Line suburb

answer.name: Ardmore, PA
answer.story: Bryant went straight from Lower Merion High School to the Lakers, making his pro debut when he was 18 years, 72 days old.

questions.prompt: Carlos Alcaraz won his 28th ATP title on Sunday in this historic European city, once home to Mozart and Beethoven

answer.name: Vienna, Austria
answer.story: Alcaraz has won four titles this season and 28 in his career, trailing only Jannik Sinner (30) and Novak Djokovic (102) among active players.

questions.prompt: Andreas Almgren, the first European-born man in 30 years to win the NYC Marathon, was born just outside this Nordic capital

answer.name: Stockholm, Sweden
answer.story: Almgren closed with a blistering 4:30 final mile to win Sunday's marathon in 2:06:01.

questions.prompt: While on a plane, an athletic director wondered why AstroTurf had to be green, inspiring this city's blue football field

answer.name: Boise, ID
answer.story: Boise State's famous blue turf dates to 1986, when athletic director Gene Bleymaier questioned why artificial turf had to be green. The Idaho school's 'Smurf Turf' became a college icon.

questions.prompt: During the '98 NBA Finals, Dennis Rodman skipped practice to join Hulk Hogan in the wrestling ring at this city's Palace

answer.name: Auburn Hills, MI
answer.story: Amid the 1998 NBA Finals, Bulls star Dennis Rodman skipped team practice to join Hulk Hogan at a WCW show held at The Palace of Auburn Hills, during the Bulls' championship series against Utah.

questions.prompt: The NFL was founded inside a car dealership in this city in 1920, with Jim Thorpe chosen as its first president

answer.name: Canton, OH
answer.story: The league that became the NFL was founded in 1920 at a Hupmobile car dealership in Canton, Ohio. Star athlete Jim Thorpe was named its first president. The city now hosts the Hall of Fame.

questions.prompt: Born in this city, Roberto Clemente won 12 Gold Gloves and became the first Latin American to reach 3,000 MLB hits

answer.name: Carolina, Puerto Rico
answer.story: Roberto Clemente, born in Carolina, Puerto Rico, won 12 Gold Gloves and in 1972 became the first Latin American player to reach 3,000 MLB hits. He died in a plane crash later that year.

questions.prompt: Born 2 days too late for the NHL draft, Auston Matthews played in this European city before going No. 1 overall in 2016

answer.name: Zurich, Switzerland
answer.story: Born two days after the eligibility cutoff for the 2015 NHL draft, Auston Matthews spent a season starring for the ZSC Lions in Zurich before Toronto selected him first overall in the 2016 draft.

questions.prompt: Nicknamed 'Rip City,' this city sold out 814 straight NBA home games from '77-'95, a record that stood for nearly 25 years

answer.name: Portland, OR
answer.story: The Portland Trail Blazers sold out 814 consecutive home games from 1977-95, including playoffs. Their NBA record stood until Dallas surpassed it in February 2020.

questions.prompt: Aaron Judge, Davante Adams and Paul George all played for this city's university before starring in 3 different leagues

answer.name: Fresno, CA
answer.story: Fresno State sent stars to three leagues: Aaron Judge (MLB), Davante Adams (NFL) and Paul George (NBA) all played for the California university before turning pro. A rare talent pipeline.

questions.prompt: On game days, this city's Memorial Stadium holds enough football fans to become the state's third-largest city

answer.name: Lincoln, NE
answer.story: On Nebraska game days, Lincoln's Memorial Stadium packs in over 85,000 fans, briefly making it the state's third-largest 'city.' The Cornhuskers have sold out every home game since 1962.

questions.prompt: LIV Golf filed for bankruptcy in 2026 after a wealth fund based in this capital announced an end to its $5B+ backing

answer.name: Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
answer.story: LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 protection in September 2026 after Riyadh-based PIF announced it would end funding after that season. The league sought new investors and a restructuring.

questions.prompt: After his '13 World Series win, Xander Bogaerts was welcomed home by the prime minister in this Caribbean capital

answer.name: Oranjestad, Aruba
answer.story: After winning the 2013 World Series with the Red Sox, Xander Bogaerts was welcomed home to Oranjestad, Aruba, by the prime minister. The island celebrated its young baseball hero.

questions.prompt: Born in a family woodshop in 1884, this city's iconic bat brand went on to supply Babe Ruth, Hank Aaron and Ted Williams

answer.name: Louisville, KY
answer.story: The Louisville Slugger bat was born in 1884 in a Louisville woodshop run by the Hillerich family. The brand went on to arm legends like Babe Ruth, Hank Aaron and Ted Williams at the plate.

questions.prompt: A catfishing scandal rocked this university in 2013 when Manti Te'o's girlfriend and her death were revealed to be fake

answer.name: University of Notre Dame (South Bend, IN)
answer.story: In 2013, Notre Dame linebacker Manti Te'o was revealed to be the victim of a catfishing hoax: the girlfriend he had mourned never existed. The bizarre saga gripped the sports world.

questions.prompt: Founded in 1923 and once named for a liquor company, the NBA's oldest franchise made this city its fourth home in 1985

answer.name: Sacramento, CA
answer.story: The NBA's oldest franchise, the Kings, started in 1923 as the Rochester Seagrams, named for a distiller. After moves through several cities, the team made Sacramento its home in 1985.

questions.prompt: The U.S. men's and women's hockey teams both beat Canada 2-1 with golden goals at this city's '26 Winter Olympics

answer.name: Milan, Italy
answer.story: At the 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan, Megan Keller and Jack Hughes scored overtime winners as the U.S. women and men both beat Canada 2-1 to win hockey gold.

questions.prompt: Yao Ming saved his hometown club in this city from financial collapse in 2009, 7 years after leading them to a title

answer.name: Shanghai, China
answer.story: In 2009, Yao Ming bought and rescued his hometown Shanghai Sharks from financial ruin. The NBA star had led the Chinese club to a 2002 CBA championship before his move to the Houston Rockets.
